[[Events|event]] before defeating [[The Elder]]|limit=6|frequency=6|stars=No}} }} == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Greydwarfs|Aggressive creature strategies#Greydwarf}} === Attack === Swings their hand sideways in a 1.7-meter 90-degree horizontal arc to scratch the player (14 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). This attack can be used every 2 seconds when within 1.2 meters of a player. === Throw === Winds their arm back before swinging forward to throw a rock (10 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] damage). The rock travels at 12 meters per second for up to 4 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 5 degrees. This attack can be used every 8 seconds when within 5–15 meters of a player. == Gallery == File:Valheim Greydwarf-1 ver0-79-10.jpg File:One-star greydwarf.png|A One-Star Greydwarf. Note the red bark. File:Two-star greydwarf.png|A Two-Star Greydwarf. Note the blue bark and accents. File:2Star Greydwarf.png|2 star Greydwarf == Notes == * The word Greydwarf is derived from Astrid Lindgren's tale Ronja the Robber's daughter (Ronja Rövardotter). Originally named Grådvärgar, which is literally translated to Greydwarves. They are short creatures with grey fur who will attack a person when they sense the victim's fear. If you are emotionally aggressive then they will leave you be. == Lore == {{Quote|Let all who read me beware of the Greydwarfs, the skulkers in darkness, the soulless ones. They are born from rot and rainfall, they spring like mushrooms from the smoking soil. There is nothing on their tongues or behind their eyes, those who fear nothing should still fear them. When the soul of a murderer or a great sinner rots under the ground, it makes a hollow cyst which draws rock and wood and moss to it. It gathers up the peat into flesh, braids reeds into bone and takes rags for skin. It should not walk but when the night comes it walks. Should you who read this see one with a sword to your hand, lance it and let it out. Or put it to the torch, for it fears the flame.|[[Runestone]]}} The runestones' portrayal of the Greydwarfs is racially motivated: they stereotype the entire race as "the skulkers in darkness, the soulless ones", with "nothing on their tongues or behind their eyes",In-game text, Greydwarf runestone ($lore_greydwarfs). and one urges travelers not to pity them: "Raised by the Old Man of the Forest from seeds of sin, the greydwarfs clothe themselves in the human forms they once knew, but there is no longer any warmth in their hearts. They live now only to serve the Elder and to protect the wood. Do not let pity for them stay your hand."In-game text, Black Forest runestone ($lore_blackforest_random09). == References == {{Creatures}} [[ru:Грейдворф]] [[fr:Naingris]] [[cs:Šedý trpaslík]] [[uk:Сіролюд]] [[de:Grauzwerg]] __NOTOC__

They are small flaming imps that are relatively weak, especially in [[Swamp]]s where the constant raining significantly reduces the damage from their ranged fireball attack. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Surtlings|Aggressive creature strategies#Surtling}} Surtlings spawning near [[Fire geysers]] can be farmed through lowering the ground around the spawn area with a pickaxe. As soon as the Surtling spawns in water, it will take damage and quickly die. === Fireball === Winds back before tossing a ball of fire at the player, which applies the [[Burning]] status (10 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 40 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage). This attack has a 3-second cooldown and can be used within 10 meters of a player. The fireball travels at 11 meters per second for up to 4 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 2–20 degrees. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Coal|0star=4|1star=8|2star=16}} {{drop row|item=Surtling core| 0star=50%|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Surtling trophy|0star=5%| 1star=5%|2star=5%}}}} == Spawning == {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=3 [[spawn points]] near [[Fire geysers]]|frequency=Respawn after 5 minutes}} {{spawn row|type=During "There's a smell of sulfur in the air..." [[Events|event]] after defeating [[Bonemass]]|limit=4|frequency=6|stars=No}} }} == Notes == * Surtling is a reference to [[wikipedia:Surtr|Surtr]], also anglicized as 'Surt', a mighty giant fire jötunn in [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norse_mythology Norse mythology]. **Interestingly, in earlier versions of the game, among [[Runestone]]s the player may stumble upon in Swamp biome provided the origin of Surtlings as demonic creatures born from splintered fragments of Surtr himself after being struck down and mutilated by First Men. * The flames around 1-star Surtlings are blue, with 2-star Surtlings being pink. * Projectiles can be parried, staggering the Surtling for some time and allowing you to close the distance for melee attacks, and possibly pushing them into water. * While they take damage from water, rain does not affect them. * Before the [[Version history|Ashlands update]], Surtlings were very common and the only inhabitants of Ashlands. == Gallery == File:Valheim Surtling-1 ver0-79-10.jpg|

 == Lore == {{Quote|Let you who read me know of the Surtlings, that you might not fall prey to their wickedness. Long ago the great demon Surtr was brought down and destroyed by the First Men, giant warriors of whom you are but a dwindling echo. They smote long upon the body of this Surtr with swords and hammers so that his fiery substance was shattered into many small pieces. He who was made of the fire was fire in every part of him. You could not say ‘Here is the brain of Surtr’ or ‘Here is Surtr’s liver’ because every part was Surtr. So all the fragments of him were Surtr still, only much weaker in power and in thought and in memory, with no way to become whole once again. Now we call these fragments Surtlings and when they are found they should be stamped out like the last embers of a fire or doused with water to choke off their flames at the root. They will throw fire from afar and joy in causing terror and destruction. Even in his scattered dotage, the demon seeks revenge on the children of the First Men.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[ru:Суртлинг]] [[uk:Вогневик]] [[fr:Surtling]] [[cs:Surtling]] [[de:Surtling]]

This attack hits in a circular area with a radius of 2.5 meters and can be used every 12 seconds when within 6 meters of a player. == Taming == ''For general taming information and strategies, see [[Taming|Taming.]]'' Because Lox tend to stay in herds and wander back to the same location, it is possible to tame large groups of Lox even early in the game by periodically sprinting through the Plains and scattering the [[Cloudberries]] around places where the herds gather. Alternatively, with a decent [[Sneak (Skill)]] (and carefully watching the player's surroundings) it is possible to sneak at single Lox (or small herds) and disperse the Cloudberries this way. It is recommended to not go below 50 stamina when doing this so the player can run away if spotted. Once most or all of them are tamed, [[Deathsquito|Deathsquitos]] and [[Fuling|Fulings]] will often attack them instead of the player. With a number of tamed Lox, there will usually be one between the player and a new spawn. However, without adequate healing, some of the Lox are liable to eventually [[Death|die]] if the area is active at [[Day and Night Cycle|night]] or during certain [[Events|invasions]]. This strategy saves the player from having to build pens for the Lox, but the risk of death is high while scattering seeds. If the player's armor does not protect them from a Deathsquito attack, it may be ideal to leave everything in chests except Cloudberries and flint spears. A rudimentary [[Shelter Effect|shelter]] with a [[Portal]] in it can be used to safely enter the Plains and to keep the area active while the Lox are being tamed. == Riding == Tamed Lox can be utilized as mounts. First, create a [[Lox Saddle]], then equip it to a Lox by assigning the saddle to a hot key and using it while close to the creature. Directional keys will not cause the Lox to turn while riding. Instead, the player must move the camera, and the Lox will always move straight in the direction that the camera is facing. A Lox can move either at walking or sprinting speed - it cannot reverse. A ridden Lox is a very powerful companion. In addition to retaining their impressive health and damage resistances, a sprinting Lox is faster than even the most high sprint-level players, while also enjoying the benefit of not being slowed down by equipped armor. A ridden Lox also completely ignores a player's carried weight, able to move and even sprint while the rider is encumbered. A mounted Lox has 240 points of stamina which drain at approximately the same rate as a player's while sprinting, however, leveling the Riding [[Skills|skill]] both increases the speed of a ridden Lox as well as reducing the amount of stamina drained. It is important to note that a Lox's stamina regenerates much, much slower than a player's, one point is regained roughly every 4 seconds while the creature has been recently fed, and one every 10 seconds while it is hungry. While it is not currently possible to utilize a player's weapons while riding (trying to do so results in the player instantly dismounting as soon as the attack key is pressed) a Lox at full sprint is capable of trampling most other creatures underfoot, dealing heavy damage when it comes into contact with them. Additionally, when not making the Lox move, it will attack nearby enemies like it would do when unsaddled. == Breeding == Lox can breed provided the Lox is: * Happy and well-fed with [[Cloudberries]], [[Flax]], or [[Barley]] * There is another Lox within 8 meters * No more than 4 Lox within 20 meters * Not already pregnant * Within approximately 64 meters of a player Additionally, in order for a Lox to be able to pathfind to and eat food, it can't be in a room with a ceiling that is too low. On flat ground, 8 meters of vertical clearance should be enough, but it is recommended to have 10 meters or more if you intend to house your Lox indoors. Once met, the Lox will accumulate love points with each other until the pregnancy starts. Pregnancy will last a minimum of two minutes, after which the birth of the baby Lox is random chance. '''Leviathans''' are passive [[creatures]] found in [[Ocean|Oceans]]. They are massive rock-type beings that have a 10% chance of submerging each time their [[Abyssal Barnacle]]s are damaged.

Leviathans themselves are immovable and indestructible; only the barnacles on their back can be destroyed by mining them.

It is not possible to build on Leviathans. 

===Drops===
Each [[Abyssal Barnacle]] drops the following when mined:

|stars=0}}
See their [[Abyssal Barnacle|main page]] for details on how to mine the barnacles.

Each time a barnacle is hit, there is a 10% chance that the leviathan will be disturbed (indicated by it shaking and emitting noise). Once 20 seconds have passed after it is first disturbed, it will begin permanently submerging into the ocean (accompanied by much more shaking and noises). During those 20 seconds, further hits still have a 10% chance to trigger additional shaking.

It takes roughly 25 seconds from the start of the leviathan's submersion process until its entire body is below the waterline. During the first few seconds it actually raises its body up higher, then slowly begins accelerating downward, eventually moving faster than 1 m/s.

=== Spawning===
Leviathans are spawned upon world generation and do not respawn once they have retreated below the depths of the ocean.

They have 1% chance of appearing on each full Ocean [[Spawn zones|zone]] and require at least 30 meters depth.

'''Lord Reto''' is a [[Creatures|miniboss]] found in the [[Ashlands]]. He is part of the sub-quest to craft the [[Dyrnwyn]].

He can be found inside the dungeon [[Tomb of Lord Reto]]. The location of the dungeon is given by following a series of 3 [[Vegvisir]]s, see [[Mysterious Location]] for details.

== Attacks and abilities ==
{{For|strategies for defeating Lord Reto|Boss strategies#Lord Reto}}
Lord Reto spawns naturally with 2 stars, so all of his stats are listed with those [[Creature Level#Effects|multipliers]] taken into account. He has an attack move set similar to a regular [[Charred Warrior]], but more health and damage than even a 2-starred Charred Warrior. He is also capable of killing a player in one-hit, even if they have got the currently max health and [[Flametal Armor|best armor]] possible. ([[Piquant Pie]], [[Mashed Meat]] and [[Fiery Svinstew]] which provides 300 health.)

=== Swing ===
A vertical sword slash that creates a 3-meter 115-degree arc in front (480 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). It can be used every 3 seconds when within 1.6 meters of a player.

=== Thrust ===
A forward stab that extends in a 3-meter line which arcs slightly by 10 degrees (460 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]] damage). This attack can be used every 3 seconds when within 1.6 meters of a player.

=== Feint ===
Shares the same windup as the swing, but Lord Reto will suddenly pause before shifting stances to attack with a different slash that hits in a 3-meter 77.3-degree vertical arc (500 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage). It can be used every 8 seconds when within 1.6 meters of a player. There is practically no difference between the animation for this attack and that of the regular swing<ref group="Note">The timing difference between the regular swing and the feint is approximately 0.57 seconds.</ref>; there is more than enough time to react and parry again, but the attack will catch rolling players unless completely moving out of his range.

=== Thrust feint ===
Shares the same windup as the thrust, but Lord Reto will suddenly pause before attacking with an upward swing from his current stance (420 [[Damage types#Pierce|Pierce]] damage). This attack creates a vertical arc that is 3 meters long and spans 60 degrees. It can be used every 3 seconds when within 1.6 meters of a player. Similar to the regular feint, there is practically no difference between the animation for this attack and that of the regular thrust<ref group="Note">The timing difference between the thrust and the feint thrust is approximately 0.631 seconds.</ref>; there is more than enough time to react and parry again, but the attack will catch rolling players unless completely moving out of his range.

The '''Moose Calf''' is the young form of the [[Moose]], found in the [[Deep North]]. It grows into an adult Moose after 3,000 seconds (50 minutes). A calf born to a tamed Moose stays tamed when it grows up.

== Breeding ==
Moose Calves do not spawn in the wild. They are born to [[Taming|tamed]] Moose that are fed and have a partner nearby, and a pregnancy lasts 60 seconds. A Moose does not become pregnant while five or more Moose and Moose Calves are within 10 meters of it.

A calf is born tamed and with the same star level as its mother. When it grows up, the adult Moose keeps the calf's star level and tamed state.

== Behavior ==
Moose Calves are passive. When they sense an enemy they flee instead of fighting, and they flee when they take damage.

* '''Horns''': 160 [[Damage types#Slash|Slash]] damage.
